questions.text: He ____ in Lahore since 2015.
questions.explanation: An action that began at a stated point in the past and still continues takes the present perfect continuous with 'since'.

questions.text: She ____ her homework before the guests arrived.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions is expressed by the past perfect, so 'had finished' precedes 'arrived'.

questions.text: Water ____ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Universal truths and scientific facts are stated in the simple present tense.

questions.text: By the time you arrive, I ____ the report.
questions.explanation: An action to be finished before a future point takes the future perfect tense.

questions.text: Look! The baby ____ in the next room.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' signals an action happening at the moment of speaking, which requires the present continuous.

questions.text: I ____ him at the conference yesterday.
questions.explanation: A finished action with a definite past time marker such as 'yesterday' takes the simple past.

questions.text: They ____ for two hours when the coach arrived.
questions.explanation: An activity continuing over a period up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous.

questions.text: The train ____ before we reached the station.
questions.explanation: The action completed earlier than another past action ('reached') is put in the past perfect.

questions.text: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the match.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the if-clause is in the present simple and the main clause takes 'will' + base verb.

questions.text: He said that he ____ tired.
questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past, the reported verb is back-shifted to the past tense.

questions.text: I ____ my breakfast when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: The longer background action is in the past continuous and the sudden action in the simple past.

questions.text: He ____ smoke, but he gave it up last year.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' + base verb expresses a discontinued past habit; 'is/was used to' means accustomed to.

questions.text: We ____ each other since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb, so a state continuing from the past to now takes the present perfect simple.

questions.text: Hardly had he entered the room when the lights ____ out.
questions.explanation: In the 'hardly had ... when' pattern the second clause takes the simple past.

questions.text: I have never ____ such a beautiful sunset.
questions.explanation: After 'have/has' the third form of the verb (past participle) is used, which is 'seen'.

questions.text: The work ____ by the students yesterday.
questions.explanation: A past action seen from the point of view of the object takes the past simple passive 'was done'.

questions.text: English ____ all over the world.
questions.explanation: The subject receives the action, so the present simple passive 'is spoken' is required.

questions.text: I wish I ____ rich enough to buy that house.
questions.explanation: After 'I wish' an unreal present situation takes the past subjunctive 'were' for all persons.

questions.text: He will call you as soon as he ____ home.
questions.explanation: After time conjunctions such as 'as soon as', future meaning is expressed by the present simple, not 'will'.

questions.text: She ____ to Karachi three times.
questions.explanation: Experience up to the present, with no stated past time, takes the present perfect 'has been'.

questions.text: This time tomorrow I ____ over the Atlantic.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a stated future moment takes the future continuous tense.

questions.text: He is not here yet; he must ____ the train.
questions.explanation: A confident deduction about the past is expressed by 'must have' + past participle.

questions.text: She avoided ____ the question put by the reporter.
questions.explanation: The verb 'avoid' is always followed by a gerund, never by an infinitive.

questions.text: I look forward to ____ from you soon.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to' the word 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by the gerund.

questions.text: It is high time we ____ home.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by the past subjunctive form of the verb although the sense is present.

questions.text: If he had studied harder, he ____ the examination.
questions.explanation: In the third conditional the main clause takes 'would have' + past participle.

questions.text: He is ____ honest man and everyone trusts him.
questions.explanation: The 'h' in 'honest' is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.

questions.text: ____ Nile is the longest river in Africa.
questions.explanation: Names of rivers always take the definite article 'the'.

questions.text: She plays ____ piano very well.
questions.explanation: Names of musical instruments take the definite article when we speak of playing them.

questions.text: He is ____ university student in his final year.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /ju:/, so it takes 'a' and not 'an'.

questions.text: I bought ____ umbrella from the market yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article 'an' is used.

questions.text: ____ moon revolves round the earth.
questions.explanation: Unique objects in nature such as the moon, the sun and the sky take the definite article.

questions.text: Children in Pakistan go to ____ school at the age of five.
questions.explanation: Institutions such as school, college and hospital take no article when referred to for their primary purpose.

questions.text: He is ____ best student in the class.
questions.explanation: Superlative adjectives are preceded by the definite article 'the'.

questions.text: There is ____ hospital at the end of this road.
questions.explanation: A singular countable noun mentioned for the first time and beginning with a consonant sound takes 'a'.

questions.text: ____ rich should help the poor.
questions.explanation: An adjective used as a plural common noun for a whole class takes the definite article.

questions.text: She is ____ M.A. in Economics.
questions.explanation: The letter M is pronounced /em/, a vowel sound, so the abbreviation takes 'an'.

questions.text: He gave me ____ one-rupee coin as a souvenir.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so it takes 'a' in spite of the vowel letter.

questions.text: ____ Himalayas separate the subcontinent from Tibet.
questions.explanation: Names of mountain ranges, unlike single peaks, take the definite article.

questions.text: ____ Holy Quran is a complete code of life.
questions.explanation: Names of sacred books take the definite article 'the'.

questions.text: She has been teaching in this college ____ 2010.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point of time, while 'for' is used with a length of time.

questions.text: He is good ____ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'good' takes the preposition 'at' when it refers to skill in a subject or activity.

questions.text: She is married ____ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'married to' a person.

questions.text: The clerk was accused ____ theft.
questions.explanation: One is accused of an offence, although one is charged with it.

questions.text: Distribute these sweets ____ the two boys.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons or things and 'among' for more than two.

questions.text: The book is divided ____ five chapters.
questions.explanation: 'Divide into' shows the parts something is separated in to.

questions.text: He congratulated me ____ my success.
questions.explanation: The verb 'congratulate' takes the preposition 'on' before the occasion.

questions.text: She insisted ____ going alone.
questions.explanation: 'Insist' is followed by 'on' and then a gerund.

questions.text: I have no objection ____ your proposal.
questions.explanation: The noun 'objection' is followed by the preposition 'to'.

questions.text: He is senior ____ me in the department.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.text: The hall was crowded ____ people.
questions.explanation: 'Crowded with' is the fixed collocation for a place full of people or things.

questions.text: She apologised ____ her mistake.
questions.explanation: One apologises for a fault and to a person.

questions.text: He is fond ____ classical music.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'fond' is always followed by 'of'.

questions.text: The child is entirely dependent ____ his parents.
questions.explanation: 'Dependent' takes the preposition 'on' before the person or thing relied upon.

questions.text: The prisoners were deprived ____ their basic rights.
questions.explanation: 'Deprive' is followed by 'of' before the thing taken away.

questions.text: The suspect was charged ____ murder.
questions.explanation: A person is charged with an offence, though accused of it.

questions.text: Pakistan came into being ____ 14 August 1947.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used with particular dates and days; 'in' is used with months and years.

questions.text: The class begins ____ eight o'clock every morning.
questions.explanation: 'At' is used with an exact clock time.

questions.text: The rain prevented us ____ going out.
questions.explanation: 'Prevent someone from doing something' is the fixed pattern.

questions.text: He has completely recovered ____ his illness.
questions.explanation: 'Recover' takes 'from' before an illness or setback.

questions.text: A true artist is indifferent ____ criticism.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'indifferent' is followed by 'to'.

questions.text: Each of the boys ____ given a prize.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' is followed by a plural noun but always takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Neither of the answers ____ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' refers to one of two and therefore takes a singular verb.

questions.text: The news ____ very disturbing.
questions.explanation: 'News' is plural in form but singular in meaning and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Mathematics ____ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -ics take a singular verb.

questions.text: Ten miles ____ a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: A plural expression of distance, weight or amount treated as one whole takes a singular verb.

questions.text: A number of students ____ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and therefore takes a plural verb.

questions.text: The number of students in this class ____ fifty.
questions.explanation: 'The number' is a singular noun phrase and takes a singular verb, unlike 'a number of'.

questions.text: Bread and butter ____ a wholesome breakfast.
questions.explanation: Two nouns joined by 'and' that name a single idea or dish take a singular verb.

questions.text: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present in the hall.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it, here the plural 'students'.

questions.text: One of my friends ____ a doctor in Multan.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'one', not 'friends', so the verb is singular.

questions.text: The quality of these mangoes ____ not good.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the head noun 'quality', not with the noun in the intervening phrase.

questions.text: The cattle ____ grazing in the field.
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' is a collective noun that is always plural in construction.

questions.text: Everybody ____ his own opinion about the matter.
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like everybody, somebody and nobody are singular.

questions.text: Not only the students but also the teacher ____ absent.
questions.explanation: With 'not only ... but also' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the singular 'teacher'.

questions.text: Each boy and each girl ____ been given a separate book.
questions.explanation: Singular nouns preceded by 'each' or 'every' and joined by 'and' still take a singular verb.

questions.text: My trousers ____ torn at the knee.
questions.explanation: Nouns naming double garments or instruments, such as trousers and scissors, take a plural verb.

questions.text: Two-thirds of the work ____ been completed.
questions.explanation: With a fraction the verb follows the noun that comes after 'of', and 'work' is uncountable and singular.

questions.text: There ____ many people in the hall.
questions.explanation: In 'there' sentences the verb agrees with the real subject that follows it, here plural 'people'.

questions.text: Slow and steady ____ the race.
questions.explanation: The two adjectives express one idea and are treated as a singular subject.

questions.text: Either of the two roads ____ to the station.
questions.explanation: 'Either of' means one or the other of two and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Between you and ____, the plan is bound to fail.
questions.explanation: A pronoun after a preposition must be in the objective case, so 'me' is required.

questions.text: Each of the girls did ____ best in the competition.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, and since the reference is to girls the singular possessive 'her' is used.

questions.text: This pen is ____; I bought it yesterday.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun standing alone after the verb is 'mine', not the adjective 'my'.

questions.text: He hurt ____ while cutting vegetables.
questions.explanation: When the subject and the object are the same person, the reflexive pronoun is used.

questions.text: Neither of the boys has done ____ homework.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' is singular, so the singular possessive adjective agrees with it.

questions.text: The dog wagged ____ tail happily.
questions.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive adjective, while 'it's' is the contraction of 'it is'.

questions.text: ____ book is lying on the table?
questions.explanation: 'Whose' is the interrogative possessive form; 'who's' means 'who is'.

questions.text: The man ____ helped me was a complete stranger.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the relative pronoun used for persons in the subject position.

questions.text: To ____ should I address this letter?
questions.explanation: After a preposition the objective form 'whom' is used.

questions.text: The students submitted ____ assignments before the deadline.
questions.explanation: 'Their' is the possessive adjective before a noun; 'there' shows place and 'they're' means 'they are'.

questions.text: One should keep ____ promises.
questions.explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'one' is referred back to by 'one's'.

questions.text: We enjoyed ____ at the wedding.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' used in this sense needs a reflexive object, and the plural reflexive of 'we' is 'ourselves'.

questions.text: Those books on the top shelf are ____.
questions.explanation: 'Theirs' is the possessive pronoun used without a following noun.

questions.text: The house ____ roof is red belongs to my uncle.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' serves as the possessive relative pronoun for things as well as persons.

questions.text: He has ____ money; he cannot even pay his rent.
questions.explanation: 'Little' with an uncountable noun has the negative sense of hardly any, which the second clause confirms.

questions.text: He has ____ friends in this city, so he is never lonely.
questions.explanation: 'A few' has the positive sense of some, which fits a countable noun and the meaning of the sentence.

questions.text: How ____ sugar do you need for the cake?
questions.explanation: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns such as sugar.

questions.text: There are not ____ books on this shelf.
questions.explanation: 'Many' is used with plural countable nouns.

questions.text: He did not give me ____ help at all.
questions.explanation: 'Any' is the form normally used with an uncountable noun in a negative sentence.

questions.text: ____ boy in the class has been given a book.
questions.explanation: 'Every' is used before a singular countable noun taking a singular verb.

questions.text: ____ of the two sisters is a doctor; the other is an engineer.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the other' shows that exactly one of the two is meant.

questions.text: ____ of these mangoes are ripe.
questions.explanation: Only 'all' takes the plural verb 'are'; 'each' and 'every' require a singular verb.

questions.text: He gave me ____ advice about my career.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable, so it takes 'some' and cannot take 'a', 'many' or 'few'.

questions.text: ____ of the three candidates was selected for the post.
questions.explanation: 'None' is used for more than two, while 'neither' and 'either' are restricted to two.

questions.text: He has ____ knowledge of Arabic and can read the text easily.
questions.explanation: 'A little' is the positive form used with an uncountable noun such as knowledge.

questions.text: I do not like ____ of these two shirts.
questions.explanation: After a negative verb 'either' is used for two things; 'neither' would make the sentence doubly negative.

questions.text: There is not ____ milk left in the jug.
questions.explanation: 'Much' is the quantifier used with uncountable nouns in negative sentences.

questions.text: He is a doctor, ____?
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag using the same auxiliary and subject.

questions.text: You will come tomorrow, ____?
questions.explanation: The auxiliary 'will' in a positive statement is repeated in the negative tag as 'won't'.

questions.text: Let's go for a walk, ____?
questions.explanation: A sentence beginning with 'Let's' always takes the tag 'shall we'.

questions.text: Open the door, ____?
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence takes the tag 'will you'.

questions.text: She never comes late, ____?
questions.explanation: 'Never' makes the statement negative in meaning, so the tag is positive.

questions.text: I am right, ____?
questions.explanation: The accepted negative tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I', since 'amn't' is not used in standard English.

questions.text: Nobody phoned while I was out, ____?
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' is negative in sense and is taken up by 'they' in a positive tag.

questions.text: There is no water in the jug, ____?
questions.explanation: 'No' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive and keeps the introductory 'there'.

questions.text: He has finished his work, ____?
questions.explanation: The auxiliary 'has' of the present perfect is repeated in the negative tag.

questions.text: Everyone has left the hall, ____?
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' takes a singular verb but is referred to by 'they' in the tag.

questions.text: He used to smoke, ____?
questions.explanation: 'Used to' refers to past habit and takes the auxiliary 'did' in the tag.

questions.text: She can swim across the river, ____?
questions.explanation: The modal 'can' is repeated in the contracted negative tag 'can't she'.
